findings.title: Users can save damaged received photos
findings.description: `done` inserts received bytes into `files`, adds this device to `p.holders`, and broadcasts `have` before `sha256Hex(parts)` verifies the fingerprint; on mismatch, it only deletes the file. While hashing, `save` can access the damaged bytes and peers can request them; after a mismatch, peers that recorded the announcement can still select this device as a source, but its `want` handler sends nothing and their retries time out.

findings.title: Damaged files reload from the same peer
findings.description: On a hash mismatch, `done` deletes the local file but no longer removes `p.lastSource` from `p.holders` or sends a new `want` to another holder. If the rejected source remains online and first in the holder list, a later drag selects it again even when another holder has a good copy.

findings.title: Unchecked peer moves reposition prints
findings.description: The `move` branch in `onMessage` writes `m.anchor`, `m.x` and `m.y` into a print record without calling `validMove(m)`. A peer message with `t === 'move'` and a nonnumeric coordinate can make the new glide in `frame()` turn `p.x` into `NaN`, after which valid moves cannot restore that coordinate and hit testing cannot select the print for the rest of the session.

findings.title: Rehomed photos drift off their new screen
findings.description: `rehome` clamps a print’s actual coordinates when its anchored screen disappears, but the new frame interpolation still pulls them toward the old `tx` and `ty`. If an old target lies outside the replacement screen, the print moves back out of bounds; subsequent frames do not reclamp it because its new anchor exists.

findings.title: Hash failures leave photos trusted
findings.description: `done` attaches only a success callback to `sha256Hex(parts)` after storing and advertising the file. If hash initialization or processing rejects, the mismatch cleanup never runs and the unverified file remains available through `save` and peer requests.

findings.title: Photos jump when crossing joined screens
findings.description: `onMessage` switches `p.anchor` immediately but leaves `p.x` and `p.y` relative to the old screen while the frame interpolates them toward coordinates relative to the new one. A valid move across a joined seam therefore renders the print displaced by the screens’ world-position offset before it glides back.

findings.title: Locally dragged photos drift back
findings.description: The move handler stores `tx` and `ty` indefinitely, and `frame` applies them even while the same print is being dragged locally. After any earlier remote move, pointer movement updates `p.x` and `p.y` but does not clear that old target, so the print is pulled away from the user’s position during and after the drag.
